messages.subject: lme4: huge problem with model comparisons
messages.subject_clean: lme4: huge problem with model comparisons
messages.body_plain:
Posredujem.

Lp, Darja

---------- Original Message ----------
From: Roger Mundry <roger_...@eva.mpg.de>
Date: October 28, 2014 at 5:21 PM
Subject: lme4: huge problem with model comparisons

Dear all,

my apologies for the mass mailing. If you are not using R (namely
functions provided by the package lme4) you can safely remove this
email, otherwise please read it carefully (it is important).

I just stumbled across a huge problem that can happen in the context of
model comparisons (e.g., full vs. null model) when each of the following
three conditions are fulfilled:
* the models were fitted using the function glmer or lmer;
* there are missing data in the variables involved in the models;
* the comparison is based on the R-function anova.
What could happen in such a situation is that the two data sets on which
the two models are based are no more the same since g/lmer (as other
functions such as glm, lm, etc.) removes rows with missing values from
the data before fitting the model. The big problem arises because for
some reason the function anova still spits out the likelihood ratio
test, even though this is completely invalid when the two data sets were
not absolutely identical wrt the response (I pasted an example below
demonstrating that). More specifically, since the simpler of the two
models involves less variables it will likely be based on more data and
this invariably makes the comparison anti-conservative (increased
probability of significance in case the null-hypothesis is true). (my
intuition tells me that the same applies when using the function drop1.)

For you this means that you have to make sure that the two models to be
compared are fitted on the exact same data. Below I show an example for
how this can be achieved. Please don't hesitate to contact me in case
you have further questions (but please don't do this by email but
approach me in person).

Again my apologies for the mass mail, but I felt this to be important
and urgent. Have a nice evening,

Roger

here is some code demonstrating the problem and a solution:
library(lme4)#load library
#create data:
xfac=as.factor(sample(letters[1:10], 100, replace=T))#random effect
xcov=runif(100)#fixed effect
xcov[sample(1:100, 10)]=NA#get some NAs into the fixed effect
resp=rnorm(100)#response
full=lmer(resp~xcov+(1|xfac), REML=F)#run full model
null=lmer(resp~1+(1|xfac), REML=F)#run null model
c(length(residuals(full)), length(residuals(null)))#the number data
points use for the two models is different
anova(null, full, test="Chisq")#compare the two models using anova
#(note that this is highly significant although there is no influence of
the covariate on the response)

#how the can be solved:
#step 1: get all variables needed (but only these) into one data frame
test.data=data.frame(xfac, xcov, resp)
#step 2: omit rows with NAs included (the function na.omit is what is
really needed here; the other two are cosmetic)
test.data=droplevels(data.frame(na.omit(test.data)))
#run the models and the model comparison again:
full=lmer(resp~xcov+(1|xfac), data=test.data, REML=F)#run full model
null=lmer(resp~1+(1|xfac), data=test.data, REML=F)#run null model
c(length(residuals(full)), length(residuals(null)))#the number data
points use for the two models is the same now
anova(null, full, test="Chisq")#compare the two models using anova
#(note that it is (usually) not all significant anymore

#the following lines show that for models run using the function glm
this problem doesn't exist:
xcov=runif(100)
xcov[sample(1:100, 10)]=NA
resp=exp(rnorm(100))
resp=rbinom(n=100, size=1, prob=resp/(1+resp))
full=glm(resp~xcov, family=binomial)
null=glm(resp~1, family=binomial)
c(length(residuals(full)), length(residuals(null)))
anova(null, full, test="Chisq")

messages.subject: vabilo na R delavnico - Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Drage faraonke in faraoni,

vabimo vas, da se udeležite R delavnice, kjer bomo spoznali R paket Shiny, ki omogoča dinamično prikazovanje podatkov preko spleta. Delavnico se bo odvijala na Oddelku za biologijo (Večna pot 111, učilnica B6 - računalniška učilnica) v torek, 16.12.2014 začenši ob 14:00 in bo potekala dobro uro. Delavnico bo vodil doktorski študent biostatistike in veleposestnik v eni osebi Črt Ahlin.

Da bo slušatelj od delavnice odnesel kar se da veliko je zaželeno, da ima osnovno znanje R-ja.

Na voljo so računalniki, tako da svojega ne potrebujete. Zaradi omejenega prostora na cca 20 sedišč sprejemam predhodne prijave do vključno 9.12.2014 na elektronska naslova rom...@gmail.com ali roman....@biolitika.si.

V kolikor boste imeli s seboj svoj računalnik, je priporočljivo, da:
imate nameščen R (http://cran.r-project.org/)
imate nameščen IDE RStudio (http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/)
imate nameščen paket shiny (install.packages("shiny") )
imate dostop do vaj, ki so na GitHub portalu (https://github.com/crtahlin/AS2014_shiny_workshop/archive/master.zip)
si na doseg roke namestite Shiny plonkceglc (http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/cheatsheet.html)

lp,
Roman

--

messages.subject: Fwd: [R-sig-Geo] First call GEOSTAT 2015, 16-23 August, Lancaster, UK: registrations are now open!
messages.subject_clean: First call GEOSTAT 2015, 16-23 August, Lancaster, UK: registrations are now open!
messages.body_plain:
Če koga zanima delavnica na temo prostorske statistike v R-ju. Predava kar nekaj znanih imen iz R krogov. Bivand in Pebesma sta soavtorja knjige Applied spatial data analysis with R.

lp,
Roman

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Tomislav Hengl <he...@spatial-analyst.net>
Date: Fri, Nov 28, 2014 at 5:22 PM
Subject: [R-sig-Geo] First call GEOSTAT 2015, 16-23 August, Lancaster, UK: registrations are now open!
To: R-SIG list <R-si...@r-project.org>

The GEOSTAT 2015 Summer School for PhD students and R-sig-geo enthusiasts will be held this year at the Lancaster University (Conference center) in the period 16-23 August (arrive Sunday to depart Sunday). The topics include: spatial and spatio-temporal data and analysis in R, R as a GIS, Space-time point process data, geographically weighted regression, visualization of spatial and spatio-temporal data in Google Earth, GRASS GIS and QGIS tutorials, and spatial and spatio-temporal geostatistics.

To register for this summer school please visit: http://geostat-course.org/2015

The registration deadline is: February 1st 2015.

This summer school is limited to 55 participants. Selection of candidates is based on a ranking system, which is based on: time of registration, solidarity (participants further away from the venue receive higher ranking), academic record, and contributions to open source projects. The registration costs for the summer school are typically between EUR 450 - 500; these cover the actual costs, no profits are made. Accommodation on campus will cost ca 35 GBP (EUR 44) per person per night (not included in the course fees). The organizers provide no funding/scholarships to participants.. Participants from ODA-listed countries (http://www.oecd.org/dac/stats/daclist), however, can apply for a subsidized price for registration costs.

Lecturers:
- Roger Bivand: Representing and handling spatial and spatio-temporal data in R: sp, rgdal, maptools packages
- Edzer Pebesma: Handling and analyzing spatio-temporal data with R
- Markus Neteler: GRASS GIS 7 tutorial
- Jonathan A. Greenberg: rasterEngine tutorial
- Chris Brunsdon: Geographically weighted regression: GWmodel package
- Patrick E. Brown: Geostatistical modelling with geostatsp
- Edith Gabriel: Space-time point process data: analysis and simulation using the R package stpp
- Barry Rowlingson: QGIS vs R - mapping shootout
- Tomislav Hengl: Automated geostatistics and visualization in 3D+T: GSIF and plotKML packages

For more information about GEOSTAT 2015 please write to:
- T. (Tom) Hengl: registrations, website materials
- B. (Barry) Rowlingson: the official program, local organizer

_______________________________________________

R-si...@r-project.org
https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/r-sig-geo
